articles.title: Google’s AI note-taking app now allows you to interact with books
articles.summary: Google's AI note-taking app, Gemini Notebook, can now pull information from the books you've purchased. The new "Expert Intelligence" feature allows you to bring titles from Google Play Books directly into Gemini Notebook, which means you can ask questions about the material, as well as generate plans, infographics, AI podcasts, and more based on their […]

articles.title: A “quantum bath” puts quantum entanglement on autopilot
articles.summary: Physicists have demonstrated a new way to entangle distant quantum bits without the constant measurements and active control normally required. The team created a “quantum bath,” a shared environment filled with correlated microwave photons that automatically pushes separated qubits into an entangled state and helps keep them there. The experiment confirms a theoretical prediction made more than 20 years ago and could offer a simpler way to connect modules in future quantum computers.

articles.title: IBM quantum computer solves classically intractable problem in 15 minutes
articles.summary: IBM and University of Chicago researchers have completed a quantum computation that leading classical methods could not practically reproduce. The system used 70 error-corrected logical qubits and finished the task in roughly 15 minutes while also providing statistical evidence that the result was reliable.

articles.title: World’s first superconducting quantum heat engine could help unlock massive quantum computers
articles.summary: A tiny superconducting engine has successfully converted heat near absolute zero into useful work, demonstrating the first cyclic quantum heat engine of its kind. Future versions could operate autonomously inside quantum computers, potentially eliminating huge numbers of costly, noise-producing microwave cables.

articles.title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles
articles.summary: As frustration over AI influencers has been growing, Instagram is limiting the reach of undisclosed AI profiles.

articles.title: Harvard Law dropout raises $6M for Blue Voice to build a ‘Harvey for police officers’
articles.summary: Blue Voice is trained on department-specific laws, local ordinances, protocols, and guidelines that general-purpose AI tools can't access on the public internet.

articles.title: Clipto uses AI to search terabytes of video and is now valued at $250M
articles.summary: The three-year-old startup says it reached $15 million in ARR and profitability before raising its latest $15 million round.

articles.title: Meeting note-taker Circleback adds a free tier to attract more customers
articles.summary: Circleback is also introducing new pricing plans starting from $14 per month.

articles.title: The US is building barriers around drones and robots, but China has scale to get around them
articles.summary: The U.S. is shutting out more foreign-made drones and robots. China’s scale means the global competition may simply move elsewhere.

articles.title: Musk’s faster path to more gas turbines comes with pollution problem
articles.summary: Elon Musk says a secretive new SpaceX foundry will let him cast his own turbine blades and get gas power online 18 months faster than anyone else — but it's a bet on a fuel source that's already triggering lawsuits and health studies everywhere his (and others') turbines have gone in.

articles.title: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining
articles.summary: Caterpillar has spent decades putting autonomous machines to work at remote mining sites. It's now bringing that experience to AI deployment.

articles.title: Debian won’t ban AI code from its Linux distribution
articles.summary: Debian voted to allow developers to use AI tools in their contributions to the Linux distribution's "development, maintenance, [and] documentation." The new policy on AI acknowledges that "responsible" use of AI can improve developers' productivity, and goes on to say, "generative AI is neither exempt from nor subject to special rules beyond the standards already […]

articles.title: New York Governor Kathy Hochul thinks AI should be ‘less evil’
articles.summary: Today, I’m talking with New York Governor Kathy Hochul, and I’ll just warn you — this episode moves really fast. It’s an election year, after all, with a shocking amount of tech policy at stake, and Governor Hochul has taken strong positions on almost every major tech issue there is. articles.title: Instagram cracks down on AI accounts pretending to be human
articles.summary: Instagram is finally taking steps to address the rise of fake AI-influencer accounts that have gotten harder to spot. It's also renaming the "AI creator" label to "AI-generated profile" to make it clear when a profile features an AI-generated person that's not a real human being. "We've heard that people don't like seeing a profile […]

articles.title: Texas Governor Abbott blocks funding for more Flock cameras
articles.summary: As backlash grows over Flock's AI surveillance cameras, Texas Governor Greg Abbott has frozen state spending on them. The move came just ahead of the publication of a Texas Tribune investigation that revealed the state spent over $30 million on Flock cameras. That money was primarily raised by tacking a $1 fee onto insurance policies, […]

articles.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
articles.summary: As audio-focused generative tools and platforms have gotten more sophisticated, the internet has become increasingly filled with AI-generated music whose melodies and vocals are algorithmically derived from the work of human artists. While some of the people pumping out this kind of content immediately own up to using AI, others have denied using the technology […]

articles.title: Trump’s EPA wants to let data centers hide their air pollution
articles.summary: Just as new data centers face growing backlash from neighboring communities, the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is about to make it harder for people to weigh in on any pollution those centers create. The EPA plans to toss out a federal rule requiring public notice and an opportunity to comment when certain industrial sites […]

articles.title: NASA just used satellites and debris to navigate without GPS
articles.summary: NASA has successfully tested a system that allows satellites to navigate without GPS by using other spacecraft and debris as landmarks in orbit. In just three days, FALCON also improved the known orbits of more than 200 space objects completely autonomously.

articles.title: Scientists turn DNA into a memory device that uses 100x less power
articles.summary: Researchers combined synthetic DNA with a semiconductor to create an ultra-low-power memory device capable of storing and processing information in the same place. The bio-hybrid technology could eventually help make AI systems and next-generation computers far more energy efficient.

articles.title: Tiny robots powered by light can hunt down and collect bacteria
articles.summary: Researchers have built microscopic, light-driven robots that can rapidly navigate through liquid, collect bacteria, and deposit them in chosen locations. These tiny “cleaners” could open new possibilities for manipulating cells and microbes with remarkable precision.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years — the screen time result was unexpected
articles.summary: An eight-year Finnish study found that children who spent more time on screens tended to show better cognitive processing as teenagers, challenging common assumptions about screen use. Researchers say the key may be balancing physical activity with screen activities that encourage learning, creativity, and active thinking.

articles.title: MIT’s new lidar chip could give self-driving cars a wider view
articles.summary: MIT engineers have found a way to give chip-based lidar a wider, clearer view without relying on moving parts. Their design uses differently shaped antennas that can sit close together without scrambling one another’s signals. In tests, the system sharply reduced interference while steering a single precise beam across a broad field of view.

articles.title: New programmable photonic chip can control how fast light moves
articles.summary: Scientists have created a programmable optical chip that can slow light on demand, giving engineers far greater control over how optical signals propagate through a circuit. The technology could provide the delays, synchronization, and buffering functions needed to make light-based computing more practical. A single chip could eventually perform several tasks that currently require separate devices, potentially reducing energy use, cost, and complexity in AI servers and data centers.

articles.title: Alan Turing's biggest AI assumption may have been wrong
articles.summary: A new book claims AI has been built on a flawed assumption dating back to Alan Turing's famous 1950 paper. Peter J. Denning argues that the most important parts of human intelligence, including common sense, intuition, culture, and practical know-how, cannot be encoded into computers. He believes this makes true human-level AI impossible, regardless of how large language models become.

articles.title: US regulator, 22 states accuse Amazon of 'manipulating' ad auctions: Lawsuit
articles.summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and 22 states sued Amazon on Monday for allegedly "manipulating" online auctions for digital advertising, resulting in more than $20 billion in overcharges for 1.2 million customers.

articles.title: Social media companies are trying harder to know which users are kids
articles.summary: 'Of the child safety measures agreed to in Meta's landmark legal settlement, no category contains more detailed requirements than its commitments on age assurance—and for good reason. No matter how well the protections work, they are of little use if Meta can't tell which users are kids.

articles.title: US to press G20 on light-touch AI regulation
articles.summary: Tech bosses including Elon Musk, Nvidia's Jensen Huang and OpenAI's Sam Altman are participating in a G20 meeting in North Carolina this week amid a global debate on how governments should address the dangers of artificial intelligence.

articles.title: 3D-printed boat advances future of maritime manufacturing
articles.summary: The University of Maine launched a 30-foot (9-meter), high-performance, 3D-printed boat Friday that researchers said could help manufacturers build vessels faster, reduce the need for expensive molds and adapt designs more quickly for commercial and defense use.

articles.title: Like a bird, this drone uses touch to grip branches and rest
articles.summary: Drones often hover in the air, noisy and whining. They can already be used for many tasks, but not when you need some quiet. Their batteries would also last longer if they could take a "rest" from time to time. But when a drone is monitoring a rainforest, its cluttered surroundings and its own gripper arm become too tricky for its camera-based vision. Until now.

articles.title: Advancing lifetime prediction of thermal barrier coating system in gas turbines
articles.summary: Researchers at IMDEA Materials Institute have developed an advanced computational modeling framework that enables the systematic analysis of potential failure and degradation mechanisms in thermal barrier coatings (TBCs).

articles.title: Apple CEO Tim Cook gives nod to founder Steve Jobs in final memo
articles.summary: Apple's chief executive Tim Cook bid farewell to the tech giant on Monday, paying tribute to founder Steve Jobs and praising staff as "extraordinary" as he passed the baton to incoming CEO John Ternus.

articles.title: New analysis reveals unexpected vulnerabilities in power grids and other cyber-physical networks
articles.summary: If you wanted to take down a power grid or a network of drones, which part of the system should you attack? Researchers at The University of New Mexico School of Engineering posed the question in hopes of developing better network security mechanisms.

articles.title: Digital-twin system detects construction hazards in under a second
articles.summary: Research in the International Journal of Critical Infrastructures describes a digital-twin system that could make safety monitoring on high-rise construction sites more effective. The system could allow accident risks to be identified as they appear rather than sites simply responding to hazards after the fact.
